The case of prosecution in brief is that on 11.11.2016 at about 09.00 AM, at Aali red light, Mathura Road, towards Badarpur, New Delhi, within the jurisdiction of PS Sarita Vihar, Accused was driving a car bearing registration No. UP 16 CT 3856 in a rash and negligent manner so as to endanger human life and safety and thereby committed an offence punishable u/s 279 IPC and also while driving so, the Accused hit the car of the Complainant bearing registration No. UP 16 Z 4042 and caused damage to the same and thereby committed offence punishable u/s 427 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (hereinafter, "IPC").

It is in relation to these offences, for which the present FIR was lodged in PS Sarita Vihar.

After taking cognizance of the offence, the Accused person was summoned to face trial vide order dated 11.09.2017.
3. On his appearance, a copy of chargesheet was supplied to him in terms of section 207 of CrPC.
On finding a prima facie case against the Accused person, charge under section 279 and 427 IPC was framed against the Accused person on 29.01.2019.
The Accused person pleaded not guilty and claimed trial.
4. Thereafter, the Complainant appeared on 17.04.2023 and stated that the offence u/s 427 IPC was settled with the Accused in the sum of Rs. 5,000.
Thereafter, the Complainant gave his statement that the offence u/s 427 IPC had been settled with the Accused upon payment of compensation.
Compensation was paid and statement of the Complainant was recorded and the Accused was acquitted of the offence u/s 427 IPC.

During the course of trial, witnesses Tasnimuddin Siddiqui, HC Manbir Singh and Priyakant were dropped pursuant to statement of the Accused recorded u/s 294 CrPC.
7.

Thereafter, PW-1, i.e., the Complainant was examined, who turned hostile, even on the point of identity of the driver, identity of the offending car and the manner in which the said offending vehilce was being driven.
The said witness, who was the only public witness/eye witness was cross examined by Ld. APP, with permission of the court.
However, nothing incriminating was brought on record in the said cross examination.

8. Rest of the prosecution witnesses were only official witnesses, such as the arrest witness and the IO, whose testimony even if taken together, would not be sufficient to prove the allegations against the Accused.
Accordingly, further recording of prosecution evidence was stopped due to prevent unnecessary delay and wastage of state expenses.

Hence, vide order dated 17.04.2023, recording of further prosecution evidence was stopped, as in the present case, the same would have resulted into wastage of judicial time, money, resources and will also cause unnecessary operation to the Accused person.

In this regard reference may be made to a Division Bench Judgement of the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi passed in the case of Govind & Ors.
vs. The State (Govt. of NCT of Delhi) 104 (2003) DLT 510 wherein it was held that: -
"...In cases where the ultimate chance of conviction is very bleak for there is no prospect of the case and again conviction in such cases no useful purpose is likely to be served by allowing a criminal prosecution and trial to continue.

vs. The State (Govt. of NCT of Delhi) 104 (2003) DLT 510
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is advisable to truncate or snip the proceedings and save valuable time of the courts.

The trial should not be continued only for the purpose of formally completing the proceedings to pronounce the conclusion of a future date."
9. Right to speedy trial is constitutionally guaranteed fundamental right of the Accused person.

The present case pertains to an FIR of the year 2017 and continuing the trial any further, when it is clear that prosecution can never hope to prove its case against the Accused person would tantamount to violation of right to speedy trial of the Accused person.

It has been held in P.Ramchandra Rao vs.
State of Karnataka AIR 2022 SC 1856 that the court should exercise its power available under Criminal Procedure Code to give effect to the right of speedy trial to the Accused.

sentences.text: Thereafter, before the start of defence evidence, in order to allow the Accused to personally explain the incriminating circumstances appearing in evidence against him, the statement of Accused was recorded without oath on 17.04.2023 under section 281 r/w 313 CrPC in which he stated that he is innocent and he has been falsely implicated in the present case.
He further stated that he does not want to lead any defence evidence and matter was listed for final arguments.
ARGUMENTS 11.
I have heard the Ld. APP for the state and Ld. counsel for the Accused at length.
I have also given my thoughtful consideration to the material appearing on record.
12. It is argued by the Ld. APP for the state that there is sufficient material on record to convict the Accused for the said offences.
13. Per contra, the Ld. counsel for the Accused has argued that the state has failed to establish its case beyond reasonable doubt.
Ld. Counsel has argued that main prosecution witness has failed to identify the Accused, the offending vehicle and have not even deposed as to the way in which the offending vehicle was being driven.
Hence, nothing has come on record against the Accused.
As such, it is prayed that the Accused person be acquitted for the said offences.
14. The Accused person has been charged for the offence under section 279/427 IPC.
The Accused has already been acquitted of the offence u/s 427 IPC vod 17.04.2023 on account of settlement/compounding.
The presumption of innocence of the Accused has to be rebutted by the prosecution by reducing cogent evidence that points towards the guilt of the Accused.
The evidence in the present case is to be weighed keeping in view the above legal standards.

16. The main witness of the prosecution, namely PW Harinder, who was the only eye-witness to the incident has stated that he does not remember the registration number of the offending vehicle and has refused to identify the driver of the offending vehicle.
It has been stated by him since the incident took place 7 years ago, he cannot identify the Accused.

Further, no averment as to the State vs . on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/98279811/
4 Accused driving the offending vehicle or the offending vehicle being driven in a rash and negligent manner has been made by him.

sentences.text: In fact, even in the cross examination conducted by Ld. APP for the state, nothing incriminating has come on record.
Thus, there is nothing to implicate the Accused person in the present case.
As such, even if all the other prosecution witness cited in the list of witnesses were to be examined, the case of the prosecution could not be proved.
17. Furthermore, it has been held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Dr. S.L. Goswami vs. State of Madhya Pradesh 197 SCC (Crl.) 258

sentences.text: that the Accused persons are entitled to benefit of doubt where the onus of proving the ingredients of the offence is not discharged by the prosecution.
18. To recapitulate the above discussion, to bring home the guilt of Accused person, the prosecution was required to prove the offence under section 279 IPC beyond reasonable doubt.
The star witness of the prosecution i.e., the eye witness, PW1 has turned hostile.
There is no evidence to link the Accused person with the crime charged against him.
His driving the car in rash and negligent manner is not proved during the trial.
Further, the ingredients of the offence are not fulfilled from the material on record.

In the present case, as already noted above, the prosecution could not discharge the onus of proving the ingredients of offences in question and thus, the Accused person is entitled to benefit of doubt.
19. Resultantly, the Accused person namely, SUNDER SINGH S/O SULTAN SINGH is hereby found not guilty.

He is hereby ACQUITTED of the offence under section 279 IPC.

On finding a prima facie case against the Accused person, charge under section 279 and 427 IPC was framed against the Accused person on 29.01.2019.
The Accused person pleaded not guilty and claimed trial.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The present case pertains to an FIR of the year 2017 and continuing the trial any further, when it is clear that prosecution can never hope to prove its case against the Accused person would tantamount to violation of right to speedy trial of the Accused person.
For offence under section 279 IPC, the prosecution has to prove beyond reasonable doubt, the following mandatory ingredients, viz., i. That the Accused was driving a vehicle on a public way;
ii. the said vehicle was driven in a rash or negligent manner; and iii. such driving is likely to endanger human life or cause hurt/injury to any other person.
15. Needless to mention, in criminal law, the burden of proof on the prosecution is that of beyond a reasonable doubt.
The presumption of innocence of the Accused has to be rebutted by the prosecution by reducing cogent evidence that points towards the guilt of the Accused.
Thus, there is nothing to implicate the Accused person in the present case.
As such, even if all the other prosecution witness cited in the list of witnesses were to be examined, the case of the prosecution could not be proved.
17. Furthermore, it has been held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Dr. S.L. Goswami vs. State of Madhya Pradesh 197 SCC (Crl.) 258
that the Accused persons are entitled to benefit of doubt where the onus of proving the ingredients of the offence is not discharged by the prosecution.
18. To recapitulate the above discussion, to bring home the guilt of Accused person, the prosecution was required to prove the offence under section 279 IPC beyond reasonable doubt.
The star witness of the prosecution i.e., the eye witness, PW1 has turned hostile.
There is no evidence to link the Accused person with the crime charged against him.
His driving the car in rash and negligent manner is not proved during the trial.
Further, the ingredients of the offence are not fulfilled from the material on record.
In the present case, as already noted above, the prosecution could not discharge the onus of proving the ingredients of offences in question and thus, the Accused person is entitled to benefit of doubt.
